title: Redefining Processes At Sub-2nm
gist: At sub-2nm nodes the traditionally separate domains of manufacturing, test, metrology and inspection are merging because margins have vanished and single-atom variation can change chip behavior; vendors across Siemens EDA, Synopsys, Onto Innovation, proteanTecs, Lam Research, Bruker and PDF Solutions describe a shift toward redundancy-by-design, multi-signal defect triage, virtual R&D, angstrom-scale metrology and cross-domain data orchestration to cope.

insights.claim: At sub-2nm nodes, traditional discrete boundaries between semiconductor manufacturing, test, metrology and inspection are merging because shrinking dimensions, rising process sensitivity and vanishing margin make these domains increasingly interdependent.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Signals a structural shift toward integrated, cross-domain data platforms rather than point tools — favors vendors (Synopsys, Siemens EDA, PDF Solutions) that can span design, manufacturing and test data over single-purpose equipment makers.
insights.quote: The lines between discrete semiconductor manufacturing processes are starting to blur at sub-2nm nodes as transistors continue to shrink, sensitivity to various processes rises, and the amount of margin available to minimize problems disappears.
insights.locator: The lines between discrete semiconductor manufacturing processes

insights.claim: At sub-2nm dimensions a single atom can change how a chip behaves, and even a routine gentle wafer probe can now damage an oxide layer or a via on a thinned substrate.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Raises the bar for non-contact/low-damage test and metrology methods, a tailwind for advanced probe-card and inspection equipment suppliers as leading-edge yield risk rises.
insights.quote: a single atom can change how a chip behaves, and even a gentle wafer probe can damage an oxide layer or a via on a thinned substrate
insights.locator: At these dimensions, a single atom

insights.claim: The article's core engineering conclusion is that below 2nm, each individual manufacturing, test, or inspection step must now account for cross-over effects on other steps, replacing what used to be siloed, independently-optimized process domains.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Implies rising integration and software spend per wafer as fabs coordinate previously separate process domains — supportive for EDA/analytics platforms that bridge design, manufacturing and test data.

themes.theme: Hybrid Bonding Breaks Traditional Chiplet Test

insights.claim: Test engineers are shifting from directly probing chiplets to using sacrificial test pads, and some customers are now performing wafer bonding before test, because hybrid-bonded structures and extra-thin dies/wafers cannot survive traditional probing without damage.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Signals a capex shift toward new probe-card and test-interface technology and higher per-die test cost for advanced packaging supply chains — relevant to Siemens EDA, Onto Innovation, Advantest and Teradyne.
insights.quote: People are going from trying to probe chiplets to having sacrificial pads because they don’t want to damage the bumps that we’re actually going to bond to. And now we’re seeing hybrid bonding, which is a super cool technology, but there’s no way you’re going to be able to probe a hybrid bond and keep it in one piece. We’re seeing some customers doing wafer bonding before test because you’re getting these extra-thin dies and extra-thin wafers.
insights.locator: People are going from trying to probe chiplets

insights.claim: Synopsys says large AI data centers are building redundant server clusters and redundant 3D interconnects, not just redundant lanes, because sub-2nm multi-die packages will have manufacturing problems that can take out many dies at once, and are adopting hierarchical per-die test servers with repair capability after packaging via standards such as UCIe.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Architectural redundancy is becoming a standard AI-accelerator design cost; investors should track UCIe ecosystem adoption as a proxy for advanced-packaging yield risk and for Synopsys's multi-die IP positioning.
insights.quote: You’re probably going to have some manufacturing problems, so we’re building solutions for redundancy. So you can have redundant clusters instead of redundant lanes and a 3D interconnect, because if you have a fault — it might take out a whole slew of faults, not just one — and then you have multi-die tests, you have to test these dies before you integrate and then after integration.
insights.locator: Large AI data centers are fully aware

insights.claim: The hot-swap/redundant-cluster approach now used for AI accelerators was originally developed for mainframes and minicomputers decades ago to reduce downtime, but was largely abandoned in the 1990s once cheap servers running Windows NT and Unix made per-unit reliability engineering less necessary.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Reframes AI infrastructure economics as reverting toward mainframe-era reliability engineering costs, which could raise the effective build-out cost of AI compute versus commodity-server assumptions.
insights.locator: Ironically, this approach originally was developed

themes.theme: Defect Detection Is Drowning In Noise

insights.claim: Onto Innovation says advanced inspection tools are now detecting millions of potential defects per wafer at leading nodes, but most of this is tool-sensitivity noise capturing surrounding process variation rather than actual yield-limiting defects.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Points to a structural need for smarter defect-classification/AI-triage software layered on inspection hardware, an opportunity for analytics vendors rather than just more sensitive scanners.
insights.quote: We are seeing an explosion in the number of defects detected on the wafer to millions of defects. Because of the tool sensitivity, when you’re trying to capture the critical defect, it is actually capturing the neighborhood and the process variation also as a defect. That’s all noise and nuisance.

insights.claim: proteanTecs says at 2nm and below the industry can no longer rely on inspection signals alone to judge what matters electrically, because the volume of potential indications is enormous and most reflect local process variation rather than real defects, so quality monitoring is shifting from tracking a single indicator to combining many data points such as process variation, temperature and voltage.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Favors platform players that fuse multi-signal telemetry over single-metric inspection tools as the differentiator in test economics at leading nodes.
insights.quote: One of the paradigm changes in how we monitor quality and health is that we are not tracking a single indicator, but a collection of many data points.

insights.claim: Lam Research says the chip industry has shifted process R&D away from iterative hardware runs and toward virtual capabilities such as modeling, simulation, and optimization, because sub-2nm process complexity involves hundreds of interacting steps that can no longer be mapped out by simply running large volumes of test hardware through the fab.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Positions Lam Research's Semiverse virtual-fab/digital-twin offering as a structural growth driver as physical process-development cost rises at leading nodes, a data point for semicap capex/opex mix.
insights.quote: The industry has shifted to virtual capabilities, and away from iterative work, to do R&D. A lot of virtualization, modeling, and optimization has happened, so I have high hopes that the types of structures and technologies that are marching toward manufacturing in these nodes are designed in a more robust way than technologies of the past.
insights.locator: The industry has shifted to virtual capabilities

insights.claim: Even with better virtual modeling, Lam Research's chief AI officer cautions that ramping sub-2nm process technologies remains challenging because hundreds of individual process variabilities must be accounted for simultaneously, and it is not certain new nodes will avoid late-stage showstopper problems.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Tempers optimism that virtual-fab tools fully de-risk node ramps; investors should still expect possible yield/ramp surprises at sub-2nm despite EDA/software gains.
insights.quote: There are so many steps in the process that you just can’t map out the full space with hardware anymore.
insights.locator: The individual process variabilities are still going to be really challenging

themes.theme: Metrology Pushed Into The Angstrom Range

insights.claim: Bruker Semiconductor says thinner metal layers at advanced nodes require metrology specs in the sub-angstrom range, with X-ray diffraction imaging (X-ray tomography) needed to detect microfractures caused by wafer warpage before they cause catastrophic structural failure.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Signals rising precision requirements and unit economics for metrology equipment suppliers as node shrink pushes process control into the angstrom range.
insights.quote: The process specs need to be tight, in the angstrom range, and our metrology specs need to be in the sub-angstrom range.

themes.theme: In-Field Test Goes Mainstream, Led By Data Centers

insights.claim: Siemens EDA's in-system deterministic test product, originally scoped in 2019 in response to automotive customers asking for better test quality than logic BiST, is now being driven forward primarily by data center customers who use periodic in-field testing to schedule preventive maintenance and cut costs rather than guessing at service timing.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Shows hyperscaler demand, not automotive, is now the primary growth driver for in-field silicon test products — a demand signal for test IP vendors like Siemens EDA.
insights.quote: I scoped out our original in-system deterministic test product back in 2019, where we had a couple of automotive customers asking us for better test quality than logic BiST. However, what’s happened is the guys doing the data centers have really taken hold of that technology, and they’re driving it forward… to save a huge amount of cash in terms of being able to understand when to do that preventive maintenance instead of just guessing at it.
insights.locator: We're starting to see a mixture

insights.claim: proteanTecs' 'Margin Agents' assess whether a temperature increase in one layer of a stacked or shingled 3D package actually creates a timing risk in a neighboring domain, because thermal coupling between stacked tiers can silently erode timing margin even when nothing inside the affected domain itself changed, something a plain thermal sensor cannot detect.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Highlights an emerging monitoring niche specific to 3D-stacked AI chips (hybrid bonding, advanced packaging), a differentiation angle for proteanTecs versus generic thermal-sensor suppliers.
insights.quote: Margin Agents allow us to answer a more important question than temperature alone can answer. They tell us how safe a specific buried domain actually is, not just how hot it is… A thermal sensor can tell you that temperature increased, but it cannot tell you whether that increase created an actual timing risk.

themes.theme: Orchestration Layer Connecting Fab To Field

insights.claim: PDF Solutions' CEO says foundries testing a wafer today don't know where the resulting chips will ultimately be packaged, assembled, and tested downstream, so the industry needs a low-code/no-code 'orchestration layer' linking PLM, ERP, MES, engineering, manufacturing yield, and design-automation data so AI can make manufacturing decisions without human intervention.
insights.speaker: Ed Sperling
insights.so_what: Identifies a data-integration software opportunity spanning the fab-to-package-to-test supply chain, relevant to PDF Solutions' positioning and any yield-management platform serving multi-die AI chip supply chains.
insights.quote: When a wafer is tested at the foundry, they don’t know where those chips are going to go to be packaged, assembled, and tested… We call that the orchestration layer. This is like a low-code or no-code way of connecting your apps.
insights.locator: When a wafer is tested at the foundry
